subject: Scope + resourcing decision: VPC & on-prem pilot feasibility
messages:
From: Samantha Woods <samantha.woods@acme-cloud.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Quick: feasibility + resource ask for VPC/on-prem pilot

Rishi, team — thanks again for the last demo. We have a one-off regulatory requirement for a customer proof-of-concept that needs either a VPC-hosted private deployment or an on-prem offer. Before we accept the POC we need a short internal feasibility check from Redwood on scope and resourcing.

High level asks from our side:
- Can Redwood stand up a VPC-private instance scoped to a single tenant (production-like) within 6–8 weeks?
- If not, what does an on-prem pilot look like (minimal infra, install window, support model)?
- Rough estimate of engineering + security ramp (FTE-weeks) and required documents (SOC2 evidence, network firewall checklist).

We'd like a concise internal note we can share with our procurement & security committee. Can someone on your side provide a quick feasibility write-up and recommended path (VPC vs on-prem) plus a list of non-negotiable blockers?

Thanks — Samantha
Samantha Woods
Head of Cloud Programs, Acme Cloud

Attachment: acme_poc_requirements.pdf (referenced)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Woods <samantha.woods@acme-cloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2026 11:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick: feasibility + resource ask for VPC/on-prem pilot

Samantha — thanks, can do. Looping in Marissa (product) and Dev (infra/ops) to draft the internal feasibility note.

Immediate thoughts (very high-level):
- VPC-private path: fastest to market if customer can accept a managed VPC in a supported cloud region. Work items: dedicated control-plane config, network peering or private link, customer VPC onboarding scripts, and per-tenant key management. Predictable infra but requires our private control plane changes + SOC doc checklist.
- On-prem: larger support surface. Minimum offer would be an appliance-like deployment (containerized runtime + minimal orchestration) with a 2–3 day install window and 30–60 day support SLA during POC. Needs ops runbook, hardware profile, and secure bootstrap mechanism.

Action: Marissa and Dev — can you take a 1–2 page feasibility (arch + rough FTE estimate) by EOD Wednesday? Laura, flagging for prioritization if this needs dedicated staffing.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Manager, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Samantha Woods <samantha.woods@acme-cloud.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Feasibility note: VPC vs on-prem pilot (draft)

Team — draft attached (vpc-resource-matrix.xlsx + onprem-ops-runbook-draft.md). TL;DR summary below for quick sharing with Acme:

Summary recommendation (short):
- Recommend VPC-hosted private deployment as the primary path for the POC if Acme can accept a single-tenant VPC in us-west-2. Reason: fastest delivery (~6 weeks), lower support overhead, aligns with our Dedicated/Dedicated-private abstractions.
- Offer an on-prem pilot only if customer has hard data residency or network isolation mandates they cannot meet with a VPC. On-prem requires 3–4x the ops time for install + a higher support commitment during the POC.

Key blockers & non-negotiables:
1) KMS integration: customer must support key provisioning with an external KMS or accept that Redwood will manage keys (ops/security decision).
2) Network requirements: private endpoints + stable CIDR allocation; no NAT changes mid-deployment.
3) SOC2 evidence: we need to provide the SOC2 control map for deployment and a signed DPA for PII handling.

Resourcing estimate (rough):
- Product + onboarding docs: 1.5 FTE-weeks (Marissa lead)
- Infra/ops engineering: 3.5 FTE-weeks (Dev + oncall support prep)
- Security/compliance review & evidence collection: 2 FTE-weeks (security SME time)
- Delivery & playbook + 2 weeks of run support: 2.5 FTE-weeks

Total: ~9.5 FTE-weeks across teams to reach POC completion on VPC path. On-prem adds ~6–8 additional FTE-weeks for bootstrap, hardware QA, and extended run support.

Next steps / asks for Acme:
- Confirm target region (we proposed us-west-2) and acceptance of managed KMS or provide KMS ownership details.
- Share procurement timeline and whether Acme requires an on-site install (we will need hardware specs then).

Marissa — happy to revise the draft after your and Dev's review.

Marissa Cole
Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachment: vpc-resource-matrix.xlsx
Attachment: onprem-ops-runbook-draft.md

On Wed, 4 Aug 2026 at 09:23, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Samantha — tagging our draft feasibility note. High-level rec is VPC path unless there are hard compliance constraints.
>
> —Rishi

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samantha Woods <samantha.woods@acme-cloud.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Aug 2026 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Scope + resourcing decision: VPC & on-prem pilot feasibility

Thanks everyone — solid draft. Two operational points from leadership:

1) Prioritization: Approve carving out 2.0 FTE-weeks from Product (Marissa) and 4.0 FTE-weeks from Infra (Dev + 1 contractor) for the initial VPC POC path. Any expansion to on-prem will require a separate approval and will trigger a 6-week program ramp.

2) Minimal deliverables for Acme to proceed: compact feasibility one-pager for procurement, signed DPA template, and a checklist of network/KMS pre-reqs. Marissa — please convert the draft into the one-pager and the checklist by Fri COB. Dev — confirm infra runbook items and bootstrapping sequence in the attached ops doc by Thurs.

I'll own stakeholder communication with Acme and will ask for the procurement timeline. If Acme confirms KMS ownership and us-west-2, we can commit to the 6-week window; otherwise we default to on-prem option analysis.

Laura Bennett
Director, Enterprise Partnerships
Redwood Inference

--
